most_informative_results: Class is not one ladder. Constitutional position, demonstrated awareness, orientation, material relation, and effective power vary independently.

The operator and gatekeeper middle is the densest visible class: these actors translate purpose, institutions, data models, eligibility, and implementation without necessarily holding final sovereignty.
The sharpest recurring class boundary is user versus represented person: action rights flow to institutional users while error and consequence can flow outward.
Capital providers may be constitutionally subordinate to founders or public hosts; supplying resources does not establish authority over purpose.
Public hosts can retain formal sovereignty while accommodating practical dependency and private operating layers.
Criticism is common; counter-sovereign effectiveness is rare. Voice, safeguards, consultation, and oversight must be separated from binding revision.
Worker collectives can acquire effective constitutional leverage without formal governance rights, but causal attribution requires decision records.
The estate is institutionally top-heavy: no represented-subject record in Wave 01 contains direct subject voice. This is a source-custody deficit, not evidence of ignorance or consent.
Tacit awareness and constitutional misrecognition remain intentionally underassigned because current public sources cannot support mental-state inference.

methodology.research_question: Within a bounded system and time window, who may define the objective, translate it, model reality, act through the model, absorb the consequences, exploit the arrangement, resist it, or compel it to change?
assignment_law: No actor receives one global class. Every assignment is bounded by system, period, and objective.
Formal rights establish constitutional position, not private motive.
Public statements may establish explicit awareness at their stated scope; they do not prove downstream knowledge.
Tacit awareness requires repeated conduct and an alternative-explanation review.
Silence or missing evidence may never establish unawareness.
Adversarial orientation does not establish counter-sovereign power.
Feedback, consultation, safeguards, and internal dissent do not establish the ability to compel objective change.
An actor may be sovereign in one system, operator in another, user in a third, and represented by a fourth.
Opportunity-seeking is not wrongdoing; it becomes constitutionally relevant when joined to gate, rights, consequence, and benefit.
Named individuals, institutions, roles, and populations remain distinct object types.
Effective power is separate from criticism: P1 voice may change implementation only if an observed outcome is separately receipted.
Material class position is multi-valued: the same actor may supply labor, capital, legitimacy, data, and public authority while retaining different rights in each relation.
A public host may be sovereign over the objective while a private vendor is operator or architect; public procurement does not by itself surrender sovereignty.
Represented-subject records must state whether the subject speaks in the source or is described by an institution or third party.

awareness_level.meaning: The current public record establishes no systemic awareness; this is not a finding of ignorance.

orientation.meaning: Affirms the bounded objective or constitutional arrangement.
